1.3 Critical accounting estimates and judgments The preparation of consolidated financial statements requires the Elis Group to make estimates and assumptions that affect the carrying amount of assets, liabilities, income and expenses and the disclosures in some of the notes to the financial statements. [#56](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000256665099-56)

The Elis Group reviews these estimates and judgments on a regular basis, taking into consideration past experience and other factors deemed relevant in light of economic conditions. [#57](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000256665099-57)

Amounts reported in future financial statements may differ from current estimates due to changes in assumptions or if conditions vary from those anticipated. [#58](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000256665099-58)

Recoverable amount of goodwill and intangible assets with indefinite useful lives The Group performs annual impairment tests on goodwill and intangible assets with indefinite useful lives (brands) in accordance with IAS 36 Impairment of Assets. [#60](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000256665099-60)
The recoverable amount of cash- generating units is calculated on the basis of their value in use. [#61](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000256665099-61)
These calculations require the use of estimates. [#62](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000256665099-62)

The estimates used, together with an analysis of assumption sensitivity, particularly for goodwill, are presented in Note 6.5 "Impairment losses on non-current assets." [#63](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000256665099-63)

Allocation of the acquisition price in business combinations Business combinations are accounted for using the purchase accounting method: this means that, at the date on which control is acquired, the identifiable assets, liabilities and contingent liabilities acquired or assumed are measured at fair value. [#64](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000256665099-64)

One of the most significant estimates when accounting for an acquisition is the determination of the fair value and the assumptions used to determine it. [#65](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000256665099-65)

While the fair value of some acquired items, such as property, plant and equipment, can be accurately measured (using the market price), others are more complex to measure, such as intangible assets or contingent liabilities. [#66](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000256665099-66)

These measurements are generally made by independent experts who base their work on assumptions and must estimate the effect of future events that are uncertain at the acquisition date. [#67](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000256665099-67)

Employee benefit liabilities The present value of employee benefit obligations is computed on an actuarial basis using various assumptions. [#68](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000256665099-68)
The discount rate is one of the assumptions used to calculate the net cost of retirement benefits. [#69](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000256665099-69)
Any change in the assumptions affects the carrying amount of the employee benefit liabilities. [#70](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000256665099-70)
The Group sets the appropriate discount rate at the end of each reporting period. [#71](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000256665099-71)

This is the interest rate applied to calculate the present value of future disbursements necessary to meet retirement benefit obligations. [#72](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000256665099-72)

To determine the appropriate rate, the Group takes into account the interest rates on high-quality corporate bonds (iBoxx € Corporates AA 10+ for the Eurozone) in the currencies in which benefits are to be paid and with a term comparable to the estimated average maturity of the corresponding obligation. [#73](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000256665099-73)
Note 5.3 "Employee benefit assets/liabilities" provides further details on the matter. [#74](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000256665099-74)

Defining terms of leases with renewal options The Group defines the lease term as the non-cancellable period of the lease as well as any period covered by an option to extend the lease if it is reasonably certain that such option will be exercised, or any period covered by a lease termination option if the Group is reasonably certain it will not exercise this option. [#75](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000256665099-75)
Under some of its leases, the Group has the possibility of extending the period during which the assets are leased. [#76](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000256665099-76)
The Group uses its own judgment to determine whether it is reasonably certain that it will exercise a renewal option. [#77](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000256665099-77)

In other words, it takes any relevant factors that provide an economic incentive to exercise the renewal option as well as the Group's five-year strategic investment plan into account. [#78](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_NONSEC000256665099-78)
